A.why: Clearest gown: driftwood bodice over an ivory A-line skirt, fitted waist, shell-fan headpiece, sparing teal.
A.fix: Slim the stacked pale sleeve cuffs that crowd the hips, and carry ivory round to the back skirt.

B.why: Good shell crest and sand palette, but a boxy barrel skirt, broad shoulders and a protruding white belt read as hybrid armour.
B.fix: Rebuild the skirt to narrow at the waist and flare to the hem; slim the belt band.

C.why: Most thematic: laced bodice and tattered sailcloth drapes, but near-monochrome salt-white blurs from above, and the side tatters splay away from the body.
C.fix: Add a driftwood or brass corset and a darker under-layer for contrast; angle the tatters back to the skirt.

D.why: Top-heavy: big pale torso over a narrow column skirt with sand tiers that read as a plinth; no waist.
D.fix: Narrow the bodice and make the skirt widen smoothly to the shin, with the tiers as its hem.

E.why: Ivory bell gown with a dark stomacher waist and just enough teal; holds on the slim avatar.
E.fix: Remove or reattach the pale bar jutting out from the hip and hem; give it a taller headpiece.

F.why: Bold corsair tricorn and good palette, but coat over a straight column skirt reads as a coat, near the leather family.
F.fix: Flare the ivory skirt, open the coat skirts at the hips, and cinch the waist; slim the sleeves.

notes: A and E are the only clear gowns from the ARPG camera. C has the best theme but needs value contrast. F's tricorn is the strongest identity piece and worth borrowing for A or E. Shared weakness: boxy, broad sleeves read as wide shoulders from above, against the brief. Judged from renders only.
